threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a bus stop sign instead of checking the app. Everyone else knows 'the 30' rolls by every 10 minutes, no need to wait.
Saw a guy on the 35 who’d bought half a dozen pastries from the bakery—said he was 'the king of midnight snacks'. A true Brixton spirit.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a cat lounging on a stack of vinyl in a Kreuzberg record shop; that’s when I knew I’d made it here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street art festivals springing up overnight, turning blank walls into vibrant galleries before breakfast.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they yearn for the days when taco trucks didn’t have lines stretching to Valencia. Now, it’s a waiting game just for a burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop crowd with a ukulele while waiting for the 19. The bus never showed, but his smile made it worth the wait.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think 'El Bosc de les Fades' is authentic. It's a tourist trap; real magic is in the quiet corners of Parc Güell at sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their unshakeable belief that a table in the sun is a guaranteed spot for a good café con leche at any hour.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it 'the market' without an article and try to grab a spot in that mad afternoon rush. Only locals know where to find the hidden gems while dodging tourists.
Caught the 37 home and the driver was blasting 90s R&B. Everyone was singing along, even the grumpy guy in the back. Just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling flaming torches at Hermannplatz while waiting for the bus, I knew I’d found home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Turkish market operating alongside a techno club, where you can grab a döner after a night of dancing. Pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only real locals know that the taco truck on 24th is the ultimate hangover cure, while the newcomers still chase brunch lines like it's a sport.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 tonight, and we were stopped for ten minutes because a pigeon decided to settle down on the tracks. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but it’s the hidden plaza bars and local art that truly capture the spirit of the neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by how they still use their umbrellas on sunny days, convinced that clouds are just around the corner.
